First, note that

$$
\frac{1}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ]^{5}}=[\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ]^{-5}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
[\operatorname{cos}⁡\phi +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\phi ]^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-5$ and $\phi =3\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ]^{5}} & =6[\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ]^{-5} \\  & =6[\operatorname{cos}⁡(3(-5)\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3(-5)\theta )] \\  & =6[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-15\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-15\theta )].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
6[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-15\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-15\theta )]=6[\operatorname{cos}⁡(15\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(15\theta )].
$$
